label: Polar Align

manifest.name: Polar Alignment
manifest.description: Polar scope reticle view and a plate-solve wizard that slews the mount through several points, fits its actual mechanical pole offset from true north/south, and guides altitude/azimuth adjustment.

altHigh: {{arcmin}}′ too high — lower the altitude adjustment
altLow: {{arcmin}}′ too low — raise the altitude adjustment
azEast: {{arcmin}}′ east of true north — decrease azimuth
azWest: {{arcmin}}′ west of true north — increase azimuth
needDevices: A mount and camera must be connected.
decInvalid: Dec must be a number between -80 and 80, or blank for automatic.
title: Polar Alignment

reticle.title: Polar Scope Reticle
reticle.intro: The dot shows where Polaris should sit on your polar scope's reticle right now. With tracking off, rotate the RA axis by hand until the real star (seen through your eyepiece) matches the dot's position below.
reticle.invertHint: Most polar scopes have no erecting prism, so a simple lens flips the image both left-right and top-bottom at once — equivalent to a 180° rotation, not a mirror. Leave this on unless you know yours shows the sky upright.

wizard.title: Plate-Solve Wizard
wizard.decHint: Leave blank to let the wizard choose a well-conditioned Dec (not the mount's current one).
wizard.recheckHint: Used for every reading while you turn the knobs. A short exposure and a small search radius make each reading quick; the radius widens by itself when the initial error is large.
wizard.startHint: Slews to 3 points at one Dec, all on the side of the meridian the mount is currently pointing at, so no meridian flip happens mid-run (a flip would invalidate the fit). The mount stays on the last point for the rechecks.
wizard.knobs: Turn the altitude and azimuth knobs the way the arrows point, then take a reading to see the error shrink.
wizard.autoHint: Takes a reading on this interval while you turn the knobs, even if nobody clicks Recheck. It keeps going if you reload or close this page.

starView.title: Live star view
starView.hint: Follows one star on the camera instead of solving each time, so the readings come several times a second. Turn the knobs until the star sits in the ring.
starView.starting: Solving the field and choosing a star…
starView.lost: The star is lost. Waiting for it to come back.
starView.arrived: On the mark. The polar alignment is within 30″.
starView.legend: Blue solid arrow: azimuth knob. Violet dashed arrow: altitude knob. The ring is where the star has to end up.
starView.startFailed: Failed to start the live view
starView.stopFailed: Failed to stop the live view
